claims.text: Acute hepatitis panel: hepatitis A, IgM anti-HAV (acute infection) and total anti-HAV (immunity); hepatitis B, HBsAg and IgM anti-HBc; hepatitis C, anti-HCV and HCV-RNA PCR
claims.quote: Hepatitis A virus: IgM antibody to HAV (IgM anti-HAV) (acute infection); total anti-HAV (immunity) Hepatitis B virus: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and IgM antibody to hepatitis B core antigen (IgM anti-HBc) Hepatitis C virus: Antibody to hepatitis C virus (anti-HCV) and hepatitis C RNA polymerase chain reaction (HCV-RNA PCR)

claims.text: HBsAg: characteristically appears in the incubation period, usually 1 to 6 weeks before illness; means the blood is infectious; disappears during convalescence
claims.quote: HBsAg characteristically appears during the incubation period, usually 1 to 6 weeks before clinical or biochemical illness develops, and implies infectivity of the blood. It disappears during convalescence.

claims.text: Anti-HBs: appears weeks or months later, after clinical recovery, and usually lasts for life; means past infection and relative immunity
claims.quote: The corresponding protective antibody (anti-HBs) appears weeks or months later, after clinical recovery, and usually persists for life; thus, its detection indicates past HBV infection and relative immunity.

claims.text: Chronic hepatitis B: the patient never makes anti-HBs
claims.quote: Patients who develop chronic hepatitis B fail to mount an antibody response to HBsAg.

claims.text: Anti-HBc: usually appears at the onset of illness; with anti-HBs it means recovery from past infection; also present in chronic HBsAg carriers, who make no anti-HBs
claims.quote: Antibody to HBcAg (anti-HBc, or HBcAb) usually appears at the onset of clinical illness; thereafter, titers gradually diminish, usually over years or life. Its presence with anti-HBs indicates recovery from previous HBV infection. Anti-HBc is also present in chronic HBsAg carriers, who do not mount an anti-HBs response.

claims.text: IgM vs IgG anti-HBc: IgM in acute infection (a sensitive marker, sometimes the only one in the window between loss of HBsAg and appearance of anti-HBs); IgG predominates in chronic infection
claims.quote: In acute infection, anti-HBc is mainly of the IgM class, whereas in chronic infection, IgG anti-HBc predominates. IgM anti-HBc is a sensitive marker of acute HBV infection and occasionally is the only marker of recent infection, reflecting a window between disappearance of HBsAg and appearance of anti-HBs.

claims.text: HBeAg: found only in HBsAg-positive serum; suggests more active replication and greater infectivity, while anti-HBe suggests lower infectivity
claims.quote: Present only in HBsAg-positive serum, HBeAg tends to suggest more active viral replication and greater infectivity. In contrast, presence of the corresponding antibody (anti-HBe) suggests lower infectivity.
HBV-DNA can be detected in the serum of patients with active HBV infection.

claims.text: After vaccination: anti-HBs is the only positive marker
claims.quote: Anti-HBs is the only positive serologic marker after HBV vaccination.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Acute Hepatitis B, Hepatitis B Serology table

claims.text: Severe confirmed hepatitis B: also check anti-HDV (hepatitis D)
claims.quote: Antibody to hepatitis D virus (anti-HDV) levels should be measured if serologic tests confirm HBV and infection is severe.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Acute Hepatitis B, Hepatitis B Serology table

claims.text: Suspected acute hepatitis C: send HCV-RNA PCR together with anti-HCV; RNA can be detected 1 to 2 weeks after exposure, while antibody usually appears 4 to 10 weeks after (up to 6 months)
claims.quote: For suspected acute viral hepatitis, the HCV-RNA PCR should be performed initially alongside the anti-HCV antibody test. HCV RNA may be detectable as early as 1 to 2 weeks after exposure, whereas anti-HCV antibody seroconversion typically occurs 4 to 10 weeks after exposure and may be delayed up to 6 months.

claims.text: Positive anti-HCV alone: can't tell active from resolved infection; HCV RNA confirms active infection
claims.quote: Because a positive antibody alone cannot distinguish active from resolved infection, HCV-RNA testing is essential to confirm active hepatitis C infection

claims.text: Anti-HCV: can mean chronic, past or acute infection
claims.quote: In hepatitis C, serum anti-HCV represents chronic, past, or acute infection.

claims.text: Early acute hepatitis C: anti-HCV may still be negative in the first 6–10 weeks
claims.quote: Anti-HCV antibody may be negative in the first 6–10 weeks of acute infection.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Acute Hepatitis C, Hepatitis C Serology table

claims.text: Acute hepatitis C treatment: direct-acting antivirals, started at diagnosis without waiting for spontaneous resolution; they may lower the chance of chronic infection and help prevent transmission
claims.quote: There are a number of highly effective direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) for hepatitis C that may decrease the likelihood of developing chronic infection (1). DAAs also help prevent transmission to others. Recommendations are to start treatment after the initial diagnosis of acute HCV, without waiting for spontaneous resolution (2).
